page: Google Cloud Platform n2d-highcpu-16 is a compute-focused virtual machine instance based on the x86_64 architecture. It features 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 8 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor, utilizing simultaneous multithreading with 2 threads per core. The instance is configured with 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 1.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. It does not include local storage or integrated GPU hardware.

Benchmark evaluations place the single-core CPU performance of this instance in the top 25% tier, as demonstrated by a stress-ng single-core score of 2693.38. Multi-core CPU performance falls within the middle 50% range, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 21558.27 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 9379.0. Memory bandwidth tests show average performance, recording 1018.3 GB/sec for cached small-block reads and 75.4 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads. Other operations, such as static web serving at 15.62 GB/sec and LLM inference prompt processing for a small 135M model at 904.0 tokens/sec, also align with average tier expectations.

The primary tradeoff of the n2d-highcpu-16 configuration is its low memory-to-vCPU ratio, which limits its suitability for memory-intensive applications or large in-memory databases. However, the dedicated AMD EPYC processor allocation provides predictable compute performance. From a cost-efficiency perspective, this profile is structured for compute-heavy workloads that do not require large memory footprints or local storage. It is suited for tasks such as software compilation, text processing, web serving, and light machine learning inference.
